## Motivation

Split [#44530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44530) into five review layers. This is layer 4/5, now based on `main` after [#44666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44666) merged.

## Modifications

Adds the independent ROCm runtime, AITER patches and validation records, ROCm image and launch script, plus AMD-specific changes in shared kernels, AITER attention, environment settings, and model loading. Includes the ROCm LDS optimization in moe_align_kernel.cu.

This layer changes **44 files (+11,551 / -41)** relative to its immediate base. Every split commit preserves all 32 `Co-authored-by` trailers from the original commit.

## Validation

- Rebased onto `main` at `d33dd0566a1a8b77bdad83b64cbc45510307052b` after PR3 merged. Stable patch ID and range diff confirm that this layer's patch is unchanged. Preserved the AMD commit's original author, author date, message and all 32 coauthor trailers.
- Updated the ROCm text config/model names to match PR3's `MuseSparkTextConfig` / `MuseSparkTextForCausalLM`, and kept only the conditional-generation architecture as the registered model entry. The ROCm model is AST-equivalent after these mechanical name/entry updates.
- Reviewed the range diff; syntax validation passed for all 28 Python files in this layer and pre-commit passed for affected files. No AMD hardware run was performed for this restack.

## Stack

Merge/review order, from `main` upward:

1. [#44664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44664) — CUDA Docker and DeepGEMM patches (**merged**)
2. [#44665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44665) — Kernels and collective GEMM (**merged**)
3. [#44666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44666) — SRT and registered tests (**merged**)
4. [#44667](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44667) — AMD / ROCm support
5. [#44668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44668) — Helion verify megakernels (#224)

The original #44530 remains unchanged as the full-stack reference.

Hi @Fridge003, thanks for the ROCm bring-up! A heads-up so this doesn't surprise you at rebase time: #45112 regroups `sglang.kernels` by operator, following the existing README rule that model-specific kernels live inside a logical group rather than in a model-named top-level group. As part of that, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/muse_spark/` was dissolved. The files this PR touches now live at:

| old `ops/muse_spark/…` | new |
|---|---|
| `fused_muse_spark_routing.py` | `ops/moe/muse_spark_routing.py` |
| `fused_norm_gate.py` | `ops/layernorm/muse_spark_norm_gate.py` |
| `fused_norm_residual.py` | `ops/layernorm/muse_spark_norm_residual.py` |
| `fused_op_tuning.py` | `ops/layernorm/_muse_spark_tuning.py` (configs under `ops/layernorm/configs/muse_spark/`) |
| `fused_qk_norm.py` | `ops/attention/muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store.py` |

Things that changed beyond the paths:
- `FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm` now takes `post_norm_is_input_scale` and `use_residual_gate` instead of importing the srt layer classes. `forward_with_ag` is gone; the model calls `communication.muse_spark_all_gather_norm_residual(..., **op.jit_kernel_kwargs())` directly.
- `FinalizePushWorkspace` moved to `srt/layers/communication/muse_spark_finalize_workspace.py`.

Kernel code itself was moved byte-for-byte, so the behaviour your PR relies on is unchanged. One optional suggestion: the kernels under `srt/rocm_muse_spark/` (e.g. `triton_sum`, the fused norm/routing variants) could sit next to their CUDA versions as HIP backends of the same ops in `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>`, so both platforms share one entry point. Happy to help with the rebase if that's useful. Thanks!

@@ -0,0 +1,151 @@
+# Muse Spark MI355X ROCm cookbook
+
+## Scope
+
+This path is independent of NVIDIA hardware. The failed mixed-model experiment
+combined the fork's CUDA/Hopper v12 model contracts with the ROCm overlay. The
+ROCm kernels themselves are validated: Plan B aiter 3D attention and FlyDSL MoE
+work together.
+
+The fork therefore keeps CUDA on its existing v12 implementation and dispatches
+HIP to `sglang.srt.rocm_muse_spark`.
+
+## Optimization ladder
+
+- **A — baseline:** `rocm/quark-mxfp4`, Triton MoE + Triton attention.
+- **B — kernel fusion:** `rocm/decode-fusion`, Triton MoE + Triton attention.
+  Adds cross-layer FFN boundary, fused Q/K RMSNorm, tuned/split-K MoE, router
+  GEMV, and pooler/unpooler aiter tuned GEMM.
+- **C — Plan B attention:** the B fusion stack with page-16 CK prefill and
+  aiter unified-attention 3D decode.
+- **D — best:** the C attention stack with FlyDSL expert GEMM/finalize.
+
+The checked-in HIP implementation contains the complete D code. Select B/C/D
+at runtime:
+
+```bash
+# B
+ATTN=triton MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=triton scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+
+# C
+ATTN=aiter PAGE_SIZE=16 MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=triton \
+  scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+
+# D (recommended; these are the script defaults)
+scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+```
+
+Exact historical A requires the `rocm/quark-mxfp4` source revision; merely
+disabling environment switches in D is not identical because B also changed
+kernel source and tile selection.
+
+## One-time aiter setup
+
+Validated revisions:
+
+- aiter: `4ad99832823dde2315b361cbd3b54b1c5c12acd5`
+- composable-kernel: `af9e1d1f1ae347c22feeb08fd2d42645075e0c5d`
+
+Images built from `docker/muse_spark/muse-spark-rocm.Dockerfile` already carry
+these patches, so this step is only for containers built from the plain ROCm
+image:
+
+```bash
+cd /sgl-workspace/sglang-muse-spark
+AITER_ROOT=/sgl-workspace/aiter \
+  3rdparty/amd/muse_spark/apply_aiter_patches.sh
+```
+
+This applies the page-scatter fix, Plan B 3D selector, and FlyDSL MoE kernels
+idempotently. Do not stack Plan A patch 02 with Plan B patch 03.
+
+## Recommended production launch
+
+```bash
+cd /sgl-workspace/sglang-muse-spark
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
+MODEL=/data/Muse-Spark-1.2-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
+PORT=30000 \
+scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+```
+
+Defaults are TP8/EP8, context 32768, page size 16, Plan B aiter attention,
+FlyDSL MoE, and Plan C disabled. The script prepends this checkout's `python`
+directory to `PYTHONPATH`, so it does not accidentally run
+`/sgl-workspace/sglang`.
+
+Confirm runtime identity:
+
+```bash
+cd /tmp
+PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang-muse-spark/python python3 - <<'PY'
+from sglang.srt.models.muse_spark import MuseSpark1xForCausalLM
+print(MuseSpark1xForCausalLM.__module__)
+PY
+```
+
+Expected: `sglang.srt.rocm_muse_spark.model`.
+
+## Correctness smoke
+
+```bash
+curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  -d '{
+    "model": "/data/Muse-Spark-1.2-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4",
+    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
+    "max_tokens": 512,
+    "temperature": 0
+  }'
+```
+
+Expected final answer contains `Paris`.
+
+Full acceptance:
+
+- GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, max 2048 tokens.
+- Required accuracy: at least 0.955, invalid answers: 0.
+- Serving: IL8192/OL1024, random range ratio 0.8, ignore EOS.
+- Four warmups and four measured requests per concurrency slot.
+
+The host benchmark helper supports that protocol:
+
+```bash
+CONCURRENCIES="4 8 16 32" \
+PROMPT_MULT=4 WARMUP_MULT=4 PROFILE=0 \
+RESULT_DIR=/home/yichiche/port-validation/my_run \
+TAG=D PORT=30000 \
+/home/yichiche/run_spark_client.sh
+```
+
+## Matched A versus D result
+
+Run date: 2026-09-10. Both used the same checkpoint, container, serving script,
+TP8/EP8, request seed, and 4x warmup/4x measured protocol.
+
+- c4: A `198.74` vs D `304.11` output tok/s (**+53.0%**);
+  median TPOT `18.58` vs `12.14 ms` (**34.7% lower**).
+- c8: A `339.45` vs D `475.68` output tok/s (**+40.1%**);
+  median TPOT `21.65` vs `15.62 ms` (**27.9% lower**).
+- c16: A `512.56` vs D `713.80` output tok/s (**+39.3%**);
+  median TPOT `28.90` vs `20.78 ms` (**28.1% lower**).
+- Both A and D returned the correct `Paris` smoke response.
+- D full GSM8K: accuracy `0.955`, invalid `0`.
+
+Raw results are under
+`/home/yichiche/port-validation/ad_cookbook_20260910`.
+
+## Experimental Plan C SWA decode
+
+Plan C in the patch naming is the optional FlyDSL short-window attention
+kernel, not optimization-ladder item C above. It remains disabled by default.
+
+```bash
+ENABLE_PLAN_C=1 AITER_ROOT=/sgl-workspace/aiter \
+  3rdparty/amd/muse_spark/apply_aiter_patches.sh
+
+SGLANG_MUSE_FLYDSL_DECODE=1 scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+```
+
+It passed a correctness smoke without a GPU fault, but it is limited to small
+decode batches and has not beaten Plan B consistently at end-to-end level.

+# Muse Spark 1.2 on MI355X
+
+This directory carries the aiter-side patches and measured evidence for the
+ROCm implementation under `sglang.srt.rocm_muse_spark`. On HIP,
+`sglang.srt.models.muse_spark` dispatches to that implementation; CUDA keeps
+the repository's existing FlashInfer/JIT model unchanged.
+
+The HIP boundary is intentional. A surgical Quark/FlyDSL splice into the
+fork's v12 model loaded successfully but generated repetitive invalid text
+with both Triton and FlyDSL experts. The same checkpoint and aiter stack
+generated correctly through the isolated ROCm implementation. Do not merge
+the two model paths until an A/B logits test identifies and validates the
+v12 numerical difference; startup and operator parity alone did not catch it.
+
+Validated revisions:
+
+- SGLang baseline: `dc2843801d02f9130feff04635803353561eb604`
+- aiter: `4ad99832823dde2315b361cbd3b54b1c5c12acd5`
+- composable-kernel: `af9e1d1f1ae347c22feeb08fd2d42645075e0c5d`
+
+The aiter revision is the `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` pinned by
+`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`; composable-kernel follows from it as a submodule.
+
+`docker/muse_spark/muse-spark-rocm.Dockerfile` applies these patches at build
+time, so an image built from it needs no runtime patching. Apply them by hand
+only when working in a container built from the plain ROCm image:
+
+```bash
+AITER_ROOT=/sgl-workspace/aiter \
+  3rdparty/amd/muse_spark/apply_aiter_patches.sh
+
+# Also install the experimental Plan C short-window decode kernel:
+ENABLE_PLAN_C=1 AITER_ROOT=/sgl-workspace/aiter \
+  3rdparty/amd/muse_spark/apply_aiter_patches.sh
+```
+
+`MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=triton` is the default on HIP. Set it to `flydsl` for the
+optimized FlyDSL experts, or `native` for a correctness fallback. Plan C
+short-window attention remains opt-in with `SGLANG_MUSE_FLYDSL_DECODE=1`; its
+aiter kernel is under `patches/experimental`.
+
+Launch the validated TP8/EP8 Plan B configuration:
+
+```bash
+MODEL=/data/Muse-Spark-1.2-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
+MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=flydsl \
+scripts/serve_muse_spark_rocm.sh
+```
+
+The BF16 checkpoint lives at `/data/Muse-Spark-1.2-816B-A42B-open` and
+runs through the same script via `MODEL`.
+
+Acceptance gates:
+
+1. Operator parity for BF16 and Quark MXFP4, including HIP graph replay.
+2. `few_shot_gsm8k`: 1319 questions, 5-shot, 2048 max tokens; accuracy at
+   least 0.955 and zero invalid answers.
+3. Canonical serving workload: IL8192/OL1024, TP8/EP8, random range ratio 0.8,
+   ignore EOS, four warmup and four measured requests per concurrency slot.
+4. Compare against `muse_moe_flydsl_20260910_results.json`; require completed
+   request counts and no more than 3% regression in throughput or TPOT.
+
+Local branch validation (`jacky-v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-muse-spark-day0-test`,
+2026-09-10):
+
+- GSM8K: accuracy `0.955`, invalid `0`, 1319/1319 completed.
+- Final `amd-support` rebase: Plan B/FlyDSL and opt-in Plan C both generated
+  `Paris` correctly; matched c4 IL8192/OL1024 reached `303.82` output tok/s
+  and `12.16 ms` median TPOT.
+- IL8192/OL1024 c4: `303.94` output tok/s, `12.17 ms` median TPOT.
+- IL8192/OL1024 c8: `474.98` output tok/s, `15.65 ms` median TPOT.
+- IL8192/OL1024 c16: `712.28` output tok/s, `20.86 ms` median TPOT.
+- IL8192/OL1024 c32: `1008.08` output tok/s, `29.88 ms` median TPOT.
+- c4/c8/c16 throughput deltas versus the recorded FlyDSL run are `-0.66%`,
+  `-1.77%`, and `-0.19%`, all inside the 3% gate.
+
+See `muse_spark_aiter_attention_repro.md` and
+`muse_moe_flydsl_perf_plan.md` for exact commands and known limitations.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Apply the aiter dependencies required by Muse Spark on MI355X.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+AITER_ROOT="${AITER_ROOT:-/sgl-workspace/aiter}"
+ENABLE_PLAN_C="${ENABLE_PLAN_C:-0}"
+
+git -C "${AITER_ROOT}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null
+git -C "${AITER_ROOT}" submodule update --init --recursive 3rdparty/composable_kernel
+
+apply_patch() {
+  local patch="$1"
+  shift
+  if git -C "${AITER_ROOT}" apply "$@" --check "${patch}" 2>/dev/null; then
+    git -C "${AITER_ROOT}" apply "$@" "${patch}"
+    echo "applied: $(basename "${patch}")"
+  elif git -C "${AITER_ROOT}" apply "$@" --reverse --check "${patch}" 2>/dev/null; then
+    echo "already applied: $(basename "${patch}")"
+  else
+    echo "cannot apply $(basename "${patch}") to ${AITER_ROOT}" >&2
+    echo "verify the pinned revisions in ${ROOT}/README.md" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+}
+
+apply_patch "${ROOT}/patches/01-aiter-fix-page-scatter-vm-fault.patch"
+apply_patch "${ROOT}/patches/03-plan-b-aiter-unified-attention-3d.patch" \
+  --include="aiter/**"
+apply_patch "${ROOT}/patches/04-aiter-muse-moe-flydsl.patch"
+
+if [[ "${ENABLE_PLAN_C}" == "1" ]]; then
+  apply_patch \
+    "${ROOT}/patches/experimental/aiter-muse-flydsl-swa-decode.patch"
+fi
+
+# These JIT modules embed the CK FMHA headers and must be rebuilt after patch 01.
+for mask in mask nmask; do
+  module="mha_batch_prefill_bf16_nlogits_nbias_${mask}_nlse_ndropout_nqscale_nsink"
+  rm -f "${AITER_ROOT}/aiter/jit/${module}.so"
+  rm -rf "${AITER_ROOT}/aiter/jit/build/${module}"
+done
+
+echo "aiter Muse Spark dependencies are ready"

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Read saved serving results without importing a GPU runtime or running a server.
+
+Compare explicit baseline/candidate globs within one experiment. Matching JSON
+metadata is necessary, but cannot establish matching code, clocks or warmups.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def load(pattern):
+    rows = {}
+    paths = sorted(glob.glob(pattern))
+    if not paths:
+        raise ValueError(f"No results match {pattern}")
+    for name in paths:
+        data = json.loads(Path(name).read_text())
+        for key in (
+            "max_concurrency",
+            "num_prompts",
+            "completed",
+            "duration",
+            "total_output_tokens",
+            "output_throughput",
+            "median_tpot_ms",
+            "median_ttft_ms",
+            "median_e2el_ms",
+        ):
+            value = data.get(key)
+            if (
+                not isinstance(value, (int, float))
+                or not math.isfinite(value)
+                or value <= 0
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid/incomplete {name}: {key}={value!r}")
+        if data["completed"] != data["num_prompts"]:
+            raise ValueError(f"Incomplete requests in {name}")
+        concurrency = data["max_concurrency"]
+        if concurrency in rows:
+            raise ValueError(f"Ambiguous conc={concurrency}; narrow glob {pattern}")
+        rows[concurrency] = (name, data)
+    return rows
+
+
+def compare(baseline, candidate):
+    if baseline.keys() != candidate.keys():
+        raise ValueError("Concurrency sets differ; narrow both globs to matching runs")
+    results = []
+    for concurrency in sorted(baseline):
+        bp, b = baseline[concurrency]
+        cp, c = candidate[concurrency]
+        for key in (
+            "model_id",
+            "tokenizer_id",
+            "num_prompts",
+            "request_rate",
+            "burstiness",
+        ):
+            if key not in b or key not in c or b[key] != c[key]:
+                raise ValueError(f"conc={concurrency}: unmatched {key}")
+        results.append(
+            {
+                "concurrency": concurrency,
+                "baseline_path": bp,
+                "candidate_path": cp,
+                "baseline_date": b.get("date"),
+                "candidate_date": c.get("date"),
+                "model": b["model_id"],
+                "num_prompts": b["num_prompts"],
+                "baseline_output_tok_s": b["output_throughput"],
+                "candidate_output_tok_s": c["output_throughput"],
+                "throughput_change_pct": 100
+                * (c["output_throughput"] / b["output_throughput"] - 1),
+                "baseline_tpot_ms": b["median_tpot_ms"],
+                "candidate_tpot_ms": c["median_tpot_ms"],
+                "tpot_change_pct": 100
+                * (c["median_tpot_ms"] / b["median_tpot_ms"] - 1),
+                "baseline_output_tokens": b["total_output_tokens"],
+                "candidate_output_tokens": c["total_output_tokens"],
+            }
+        )
+    return {
+        "scope": "Saved results only; no new measurements",
+        "unverified": [
+            "code/installed kernel hashes",
+            "warmup protocol",
+            "GPU isolation and clocks",
+            "identical input requests",
+            "statistical significance",
+        ],
+        "results": results,
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--baseline", required=True, help="Quoted JSON glob")
+    parser.add_argument("--candidate", required=True, help="Quoted JSON glob")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    try:
+        result = compare(load(args.baseline), load(args.candidate))
+    except (ValueError, OSError) as exc:
+        parser.exit(1, f"Audit failed: {exc}\n")
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Muse MoE FlyDSL performance plan
+
+## Attribution and current evidence
+
+`GEMM2_BLOCK_N=256` applies only to MXFP4 when `128 < M <= 1024`. Since decode
+has `M == concurrency`, concurrency 4--128 is unchanged from `a29522f`. M=128
+at 234.9 versus 235.1 us is noise. The attributable microbenchmark changes are
+M=256 264.3 -> 259.3 us (-1.9%), M=512 321.9 -> 306.0 (-4.9%), and M=1024
+450.9 -> 411.3 (-8.8%). These also represent chunked-prefill batch shapes.
+
+The cancelled end-to-end run stopped in the first discarded concurrency-4
+point and left a zero-valued JSON, so it supplies no result. Keep result sets
+versioned separately: the pre-pipeline factorial data and the later pipeline
+data are different implementations. Full-stack D-versus-A changes also cannot
+be attributed to this MoE selector.
+
+One later recorded pipeline end-to-end A/B shows different priorities by format
+(the saved JSON does not establish the currently installed kernel revision):
+MXFP4 improves throughput versus Triton by +12.0/+3.4/+2.9% at concurrency
+4/8/16, while BF16 regresses -3.4/-4.0/-2.7%. Therefore BF16 low concurrency
+is the first production target; MXFP4 needs a route-distribution stability gate
+so an optimization does not give back its present end-to-end win.
+
+## 2026-09-10 matched BF16 A/B
+
+Using the current installed aiter source and a fresh private FlyDSL cache,
+Triton and FlyDSL were served separately with the same Plan B attention,
+TP8/EP8, IL8192/OL1024, and matching warmup/request schedules. The BF16
+candidate (BN64, GEMM1 K-unroll 2, GEMM2 K-unroll 4) was enabled only for
+`8 <= M <= 16`.
+
+| concurrency | Triton tok/s | FlyDSL tok/s | throughput delta | Triton TPOT | FlyDSL TPOT |
+|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 4 | 212.30 | 208.96 | -1.6% | 17.48 ms | 17.66 ms |
+| 8 | 321.88 | 337.93 | +5.0% | 23.43 ms | 21.95 ms |
+| 16 | 474.26 | 496.86 | +4.8% | 32.12 ms | 30.09 ms |
+
+The M=4 candidate was rejected because it remained below Triton. The M=8/16
+results are one matched run per point and need repeat runs before shipping.
+MXFP4 was not changed by this selector branch and passed a fresh operator sweep
+at M=4/8/16/128/256 with randomized E8M0 scales.
+
+## 2026-09-10 final split-K result
+
+The M=4 gap came from Triton's split-K=4 path rather than its ordinary grouped
+GEMM. Disabling Triton split-K moved its one-local-route operator time from about
+96 to 105.6 us, behind FlyDSL at 99.4 us. The effect grows on dense EP ranks:
+with 8 local routes Triton split-K measured 216.7 us versus 265.9 us without it.
+
+FlyDSL now splits each BF16 M<=4 GEMM into four FP32 K partials. A FlyDSL kernel
+reduces gate/up before SiLU, and the existing FlyDSL finalize reduces the down
+partials. Split-K changes the best GEMM shape: BN16 and K-unroll 4 create
+one-wave workgroups and enough N/K parallelism to fill the device. The finalize
+uses separate LDS sum cells for each routing slot, removing the second barrier
+that was previously needed before reusing four shared cells. This reduced its
+profiled split-K time from 20.0 to 15.9 us.
+
+The strict operator sweep passed against Triton at BF16 M=4 for 1/2/4/8 local
+routes. FlyDSL measured 87.58/107.91/141.36/214.52 us versus Triton
+95.89/113.51/146.55/217.11 us. Random-scale MXFP4 correctness also passed at
+M=4/8/16 for the same four routing distributions.
+
+Fresh matched end-to-end runs used Plan B attention, TP8/EP8, IL8192/OL1024,
+and four warmups plus four measured requests per concurrency slot:
+
+| dtype | conc | Triton tok/s | FlyDSL tok/s | throughput | Triton TPOT | FlyDSL TPOT |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| BF16 | 4 | 227.90 | 229.33 | +0.63% | 16.39 ms | 16.16 ms |
+| BF16 | 8 | 345.32 | 350.90 | +1.62% | 21.63 ms | 21.43 ms |
+| BF16 | 16 | 478.71 | 511.28 | +6.80% | 30.92 ms | 29.58 ms |
+| MXFP4 | 4 | 271.93 | 305.98 | +12.52% | 13.53 ms | 12.09 ms |
+| MXFP4 | 8 | 470.65 | 483.56 | +2.74% | 15.71 ms | 15.38 ms |
+| MXFP4 | 16 | 693.96 | 713.61 | +2.83% | 21.20 ms | 20.89 ms |
+
+All six points completed their full request counts. Exact JSON paths, TTFT/E2E,
+source hashes and percentage calculations are recorded in
+`docs/muse_moe_flydsl_20260910_results.json`.
+
+## Experiments that preserve numerical behavior
+
+For MXFP4, test direct packed global-to-LDS staging. The old LDS path loads via
+VGPR and then stores to LDS, adding register pressure and DS traffic. Reuse the
+BF16 path's proven `BufferCopyLDS128b` primitive for packed bytes, then load the
+lane-specific dword from LDS and retain the current E8M0 decode, BF16 MFMA and
+accumulation order. Decouple LDS BK from register unroll: at BM16, double-buffer
+BK64/BK128 uses 21/42 KiB for both GEMM1 BN128 and GEMM2 BN256; BK512 is
+168 KiB and exceeds a 160 KiB/CU LDS budget by itself.
+
+For BF16, do not assume that the existing double-buffer pipeline helps decode.
+The recorded pipeline probe ran no tests and printed no timing rows; VGPR stayed
+166, which establishes neither a speedup nor a regression. Build a stage-specific
+harness that varies GEMM1 and GEMM2 independently: register transpose versus
+direct LDS, BN32/64/128, 4 versus 8 waves, and one versus two LDS stages. Start
+with the current low-M selector as control and preserve BF16 MFMA and accumulation
+order. The first goal is to explain the end-to-end regression by stage and worst
+EP rank, not to promise a bandwidth or occupancy target.
+
+BF16 has a much larger LDS cost: the same BM16/BN128 gate-up or BN256 down
+geometry consumes 68/136/544 KiB at double-buffered BK64/128/512. Its feasible
+LDS sweep therefore needs BK16/BK32 or narrower BN, and must include the register
+path as a control. Resource arithmetic alone cannot predict occupancy because
+VGPRs and allocation granularity can become the binding limit.
+
+The checked-in source proves direct BF16 global-to-LDS API usage, but does not
+prove the packed MXFP4 copy tiling and byte offsets. A production kernel change
+would be speculative until an isolated compile shows correct address spaces and
+ISA. The implementation should remain an experiment until all gates pass.
+
+There are three distinct versions to preserve during comparison: patch 04, the
+installed kernel, and each candidate. The installed GEMM has an extra BF16
+register software pipeline (`pipelined = (mxfp4_reg or bf16_reg) ...`) that is
+absent from patch 04 (`mxfp4_reg` only); their source hashes differ while the
+finalize source matches. Do not synchronize or overwrite the live install.
+Compile named copies into private caches and record each source hash.
+
+CPU-safe preparation and GPU acceptance gates:
+
+1. Use `tools/validate_muse_moe_flydsl_plan.py` to syntax-check without imports,
+   verify MXFP4 and BF16 unchanged boundaries against `a29522f`, check the
+   intentional BF16 M=8/16 override and wide MXFP4 override, and calculate stage
+   footprints.
+   `--emit-manifest` also emits argv arrays for a CPU-generated, stage-specific
+   BF16 control/BN sweep over production E32/top-k-8 routing cases; it does not
+   execute them.
+2. In a private container and compile cache, compile each stage/config and record
+   LDS, VGPR, SGPR, waves/SIMD, spills and VMEM/DS ISA. For packed LDS, require a
+   direct buffer-to-LDS sequence rather than VMEM-to-VGPR plus DS writes.
+3. Compare each stage with fixed routing distributions (1/2/4/8 local slots and
+   all-local), M=1/4/8/16/32/64/128/256, randomized E8M0 scales for MXFP4, graph
+   replay, warmups, median and tail. Require current correctness tolerances and
+   output sentinels; reject regressions outside measured noise at adjacent M.
+4. Only then run fixed-length end-to-end A/B with adequate per-slot warmups and
+   concurrency 4/8/16/64/128/256. Use a fresh result path and reject incomplete
+   or zero-valued JSON. Native activation quantization additionally requires the
+   full gsm8k accuracy gate.
+
+GPU work requires an explicit exclusive lease or scheduler job. Zero VRAM or an
+empty process list in this namespace does not prove host-idle status. Do not
+replace kernels in running containers or shared caches. The existing `e2e_ab.sh`
+uses a global `pkill -9 -f sglang::` cleanup and is unsafe to run alongside other
+benchmarks; an isolated runner must terminate only PIDs it started.
+
+`ds_read_b64_tr_b4` is a plausible packed-tile consumer, and a CPU-only gfx950
+`llvm-mc` probe confirms that the installed assembler accepts the opcode. This
+only proves instruction availability. The CDNA4 ISA also requires full EXEC,
+aligned addresses and even destination registers, so it does not establish a
+correct FlyDSL lane layout. See the [CDNA4 ISA](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/amd-instinct-cdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
+section 11.4 and the [FlyDSL tuning guide](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/FlyDSL/en/latest/kernel_tuning_guide.html).
+
+## Native FP4 result already rules out shipping that probe
+
+The native-FP4 probe is neither correct nor a general performance win. Gate/up
+slowed 131.9 -> 133.8 and 132.4 -> 137.2 us; down improved 63.1 -> 58.8 and
+67.4 -> 61.1 us, but max absolute error was 0.47--2.28 and relative error
+1.02--1.54. VGPR increased 394 -> 452. It should remain a research branch until
+activation quantization, lane layout and scale semantics pass kernel references;
+then it still requires gsm8k because activation quantization changes numerics.

+# Muse Spark：AITER attention 的 page-size 16 路徑
+
+這份文件重建並驗證三種配置：
+
+- **Plan A**：AITER CK paged prefill + Triton decode
+- **Plan B**：AITER CK paged prefill + AITER unified-attention 3D decode，
+  Muse 的 46 個 SWA layer 與 16 個 global layer 都走 3D
+- **Plan C**：Plan B 的 page16 CK prefill 與 global-layer 3D decode 不變，
+  46 個 SWA decode 改走 FlyDSL split-K paged GQA（`mfma_pv` + `parallel` reduce）
+
+## 補丁結構
+
+`01` 是 A/B/C 都必須套的 segmentation fault 修復。`02` 和 `03` 是互斥的
+路徑選擇。Plan C 疊在 Plan B 上面，再套 FlyDSL 兩個補丁。`04` 與 attention
+路徑無關：乾淨 aiter `c16d44b9` 要跑 `MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=flydsl` 時必須套。
+
+```text
+patches/01-aiter-fix-page-scatter-vm-fault.patch
+  target: aiter（內含 composable_kernel submodule 路徑）
+  三條路徑都必要。修掉 gfx950 上 CK batch-prefill 的 page gather VM fault。
+
+patches/02-plan-a-aiter-prefill-triton-decode.patch
+  target: sglang
+  Plan A。page16 paged prefill metadata + decode 自動路由到 Triton。
+
+patches/03-plan-b-aiter-unified-attention-3d.patch
+  target: sglang 與 aiter（同一個檔案，分兩次套）
+  Plan B。page16 paged prefill metadata + SWA decode 改走 3D split-K kernel。
+  Plan C 也需要這份（CK prefill + global layer 3D）。
+

+## 為什麼 01 不能省略
+
+`fmha_batch_prefill` 有三種 KV load 分支。`page_block_size < kN0` 時（Muse
+是 `16 < 128`）會走 Case 3 的 `BUFFER_LOAD`：整個 K/V pool 只用一個 SRD，
+page 身分編在 32-bit voffset 裡。在 gfx950 上，即使每個位址都在界內，
+scatter 到不連續 page id 的 gather 仍會觸發 GPU VM fault，對外通常表現成
+worker 消失或 segmentation fault。upstream #10180 已經因為同樣原因把
+`page_block_size == 1` 固定改用 `GLOBAL_LOAD_LDS`，而 #9214 的
+`lo32 + pool_size` 檢查抓不到 scatter 這種情況。
+
+補丁 `01` 把整個 Case 3 分支固定成 `GLOBAL_LOAD_LDS`，只留下 per-page
+rebased 的 `BUFFER_LOAD`（`page_block_size >= kN0`）不動。代價大約是 9%
+prefill throughput，但這是目前唯一已知能承受 prefix cache 與高並發的組合。

+Fix gfx950 VM fault in Aiter CK batch-prefill page gather
+
+Target repo: aiter (applies into the composable_kernel submodule)
+    git -C $AITER_ROOT apply patches/01-aiter-fix-page-scatter-vm-fault.patch
+    # then rebuild aiter so the CK FMHA sources are recompiled
+
+Required by both Plan A and Plan B. Without it, --attention-backend aiter dies
+with a GPU VM fault (surfaces as a worker segmentation fault) once prefix cache
+reuse makes the prefill page ids non-contiguous.
+
+fmha_batch_prefill has three KV-load arms. When page_block_size < kN0 (Muse
+Spark: page_size=16 vs kN0=128) it takes the Case 3 BUFFER_LOAD arm, which
+covers the entire K/V pool with a single SRD and encodes page identity in a
+32-bit voffset. That gather faults on gfx950 for scattered page ids even when
+every address is in bounds; upstream #10180 already forced GLOBAL_LOAD_LDS for
+page_block_size == 1 for the same reason, and #9214's lo32+pool_size guard does
+not catch the scattered case. This forces GLOBAL_LOAD_LDS for the whole Case 3
+arm, leaving the per-page rebased BUFFER_LOAD path (page_block_size >= kN0)
+untouched. Costs roughly 9% prefill throughput and is the only known safe
+configuration.
+diff --git a/3rdparty/composable_kernel/example/ck_tile/01_fmha/fmha_fwd.hpp b/3rdparty/composable_kernel/example/ck_tile/01_fmha/fmha_fwd.hpp
+index 50ba8ffb6..65b6591ec 100644
+--- a/3rdparty/composable_kernel/example/ck_tile/01_fmha/fmha_fwd.hpp
++++ b/3rdparty/composable_kernel/example/ck_tile/01_fmha/fmha_fwd.hpp
+@@ -701,31 +701,21 @@ fmha_batch_prefill_select_kv_load_mode(ck_tile::index_t page_block_size,
+     if(page_block_size >= kN0)
+         return ck_tile::BlockAttentionKVCacheLoadModeEnum::BUFFER_LOAD;
+
+-    // Maximum byte offsets that buffer_load will add to K/V base pointers.
+-    // Each page is addressed as page_id * batch_stride * element_bytes.
+-    const auto k_pool_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(num_total_pages) *
+-                              static_cast<uint64_t>(batch_stride_k) *
+-                              static_cast<uint64_t>(element_bytes);
+-    const auto v_pool_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(num_total_pages) *
+-                              static_cast<uint64_t>(batch_stride_v) *
+-                              static_cast<uint64_t>(element_bytes);
+-
+-    // Low 32 bits of each base VA. K and V are independently allocated and may
+-    // have different low-32 values, so both are checked. Compare against
+-    // INT32_MAX (not UINT32_MAX): the low32 bits themselves are unsigned, but the
+-    // voffset they are added to is signed int32, so the effective address is
+-    // already wrong once base[31:0] + pool crosses 0x7FFFFFFF. A sum in the
+-    // (2GB, 4GB] range still fits in 32 unsigned bits but has passed the signed
+-    // wrap point - that is exactly the band this check must route to global load.
+-    const auto k_lo32 =
+-        static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(k_base_ptr)) & 0xFFFFFFFFULL;
+-    const auto v_lo32 =
+-        static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(v_base_ptr)) & 0xFFFFFFFFULL;
+-    const bool srd_would_overflow =

++def build_splitk_silu(I, split_k):
++    """Reduce FP32 gate/up K-split partials and materialize BF16 SiLU*up."""
++    threads = 256
++    vec = 4
++    block_n = threads * vec
++    nblocks = (I + block_n - 1) // block_n
++
++    @flyc.kernel(name="muse_moe_splitk_silu_flydsl")
++    def kernel(partials: fx.Tensor, out: fx.Tensor, rows: fx.Int32):
++        pid = fx.block_idx.x
++        tid = fx.thread_idx.x
++        row = pid // nblocks
++        col = (pid % nblocks) * block_n + tid * vec
++        pr = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(
++            partials,
++            num_records_bytes=_to_raw(split_k * rows * 2 * I * 4),
++        )
++        outr = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(
++            out, num_records_bytes=_to_raw(rows * I * 2)
++        )
++        gate = [arith.constant(0.0, type=T.f32) for _ in range(vec)]
++        up = [arith.constant(0.0, type=T.f32) for _ in range(vec)]
++        for sk in range_constexpr(split_k):
++            base = sk * rows * (2 * I) + row * (2 * I) + col
++            gate_raw = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                pr, base, vec_width=vec, dtype=T.f32, mask=_to_raw(col < I)
++            )
++            up_raw = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                pr, base + I, vec_width=vec, dtype=T.f32, mask=_to_raw(col < I)
++            )
++            gate_vec = fx.Vector(gate_raw, shape=vec, dtype=fx.Float32)
++            up_vec = fx.Vector(up_raw, shape=vec, dtype=fx.Float32)
++            gate = [arith.addf(gate[j], _to_raw(gate_vec[j])) for j in range(vec)]
++            up = [arith.addf(up[j], _to_raw(up_vec[j])) for j in range(vec)]
++        values = []
++        for j in range_constexpr(vec):
++            exp = fx.rocdl.exp2(
++                T.f32,
++                arith.mulf(
++                    gate[j], arith.constant(-1.4426950408889634, type=T.f32)
++                ),
++            )
++            sigmoid = arith.divf(
++                arith.constant(1.0, type=T.f32),
++                arith.addf(arith.constant(1.0, type=T.f32), exp),
++            )
++            values.append(
++                arith.truncf(T.bf16, arith.mulf(arith.mulf(gate[j], sigmoid), up[j]))
++            )
++        packed = _to_raw(fx.Vector.from_elements(values, fx.BFloat16))
++        buffer_ops.buffer_store(
++            packed, outr, row * I + col, mask=_to_raw(col < I)
++        )
++
++    @flyc.jit
++    def launch(
++        partials: fx.Tensor,
++        out: fx.Tensor,
++        rows: fx.Int32,
++        grid_x: fx.Int32,
++        stream: fx.Stream,
++    ):
++        kernel(partials, out, rows).launch(
++            grid=(fx.Int64(grid_x), 1, 1), block=(threads, 1, 1), stream=stream
++        )
++
++    return launch

++def build_finalize(H, topk, has_norm, has_scale, weight_dtype="bf16", split_k=1):
++    threads = 256
++    vec = 4 if H % 4 == 0 else 1
++    chunks = (H + threads * vec - 1) // (threads * vec)
++    elems = chunks * vec
++    weight_bytes = 4 if weight_dtype == "fp32" else 2
++
++    @fx.struct
++    class Shared:
++        # Give every routing slot its own four-wave reduction cells. This
++        # removes the second barrier that was only needed before reusing the
++        # same cells for the next slot.
++        sums: fx.Array[fx.Float32, topk * 4, 16]
++
++    def wave_sum(value):
++        for shift in (32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1):
++            peer = _to_raw(ArithValue(value).shuffle_xor(shift, 64))
++            value = arith.addf(value, peer)
++        return value
++
++    @flyc.kernel(name="muse_moe_finalize_vector_flydsl")
++    def kernel(
++        y: fx.Tensor,
++        gamma: fx.Tensor,

++        one = arith.constant(1.0, type=T.f32)

++            num_records_bytes=_to_raw(

++        )
++        sr = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(scores, max_size=True)
++        ir = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(ids, max_size=True)
++        outr = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(

++                        v = arith.extf(T.f32, v)

++                    if fx.const_expr(weight_dtype != "fp32"):

++            slot = m * topk + fx.Int32(arith.index_cast(T.i32, _to_raw(slot_i)))

++            if (e >= local_start) & (e < local_start + num_local):
++                sc = buffer_ops.buffer_load(sr, slot, vec_width=1, dtype=T.f32)
++                values = []
++                ss = zero
++                for chunk in range_constexpr(chunks):
++                    h = tid * vec + chunk * threads * vec
++                    if fx.const_expr(split_k > 1):
++                        partial = [zero for _ in range(vec)]
++                        for sk in range_constexpr(split_k):
++                            raw = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                                yr,

++                                vec_width=vec,
++                                dtype=T.f32,
++                                mask=_to_raw(h < H),
++                            )
++                            vector = fx.Vector(raw, shape=vec, dtype=fx.Float32)
++                            partial = [
++                                arith.addf(partial[j], _to_raw(vector[j]))
++                                for j in range(vec)
++                            ]
++                        vector = partial
++                    else:
++                        raw = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                            yr,
++                            slot * H + h,
++                            vec_width=vec,
++                            dtype=T.bf16,
++                            mask=_to_raw(h < H),
++                        )
++                        vector = (
++                            fx.Vector(raw, shape=vec, dtype=fx.BFloat16)
++                            if vec > 1
++                            else [raw]
++                        )
++                    for j in range_constexpr(vec):
++                        value = (
++                            arith.extf(
++                                T.f32, arith.truncf(T.bf16, _to_raw(vector[j]))
++                            )
++                            if split_k > 1
++                            else arith.extf(T.f32, _to_raw(vector[j]))
++                        )
++                        if fx.const_expr(has_norm and has_scale):
++                            value = arith.extf(
++                                T.f32,
++                                arith.truncf(
++                                    T.bf16, arith.mulf(value, scales[chunk * vec + j])
++                                ),
++                            )
++                        values.append(value)
++                        ss = arith.addf(ss, arith.mulf(value, value))
++                if fx.const_expr(has_norm):
++                    ss = wave_sum(ss)
++                    slot_base = fx.Int32(
++                        arith.index_cast(T.i32, _to_raw(slot_i))
++                    ) * 4
++                    if lane == 0:

++"""FlyDSL split-K paged GQA decode prototype for Muse Spark on gfx950.
++
++This intentionally targets only the deployed Muse shape:
++  BF16, q_len=1, GQA=8, head_dim=64, page_size=16.
++
++Stage 1 launches one wave64 per (batch, kv_head, 64-token KV segment). A wave
++keeps all eight GQA query-head accumulators, so K/V are loaded once and shared
++by the eight Q heads. Stage 2 reduces 32 segments (the Muse 2048-token SWA
++window) and writes BF16 output. Full-attention layers keep aiter's existing
++3D kernel, which is already split-K.

++import math

++PAGE_SIZE = 16
++GQA = 8
++DEFAULT_NUM_SPLITS = 32

++def _build_launcher(num_splits: int, segment_size: int):

++    def wave_sum(x):
++        value = _to_raw(x)
++        for shift in (32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1):
++            peer = _to_raw(ArithValue(value).shuffle_xor(shift, BLOCK_THREADS))
++            value = arith.AddFOp(value, peer, fastmath=fm_fast).result
++        return value
++

++        f32 = T.f32
++        return fx.rocdl.exp2(

++        )

++    @flyc.kernel(name="muse_paged_gqa_decode_stage2_flydsl")
++    def stage2(
++        partial_out: fx.Tensor,
++        partial_max: fx.Tensor,
++        partial_sum: fx.Tensor,
++        output: fx.Tensor,
++        batch_size: Int32,
++        num_kv_heads: Int32,
++    ):
++        f32 = T.f32
++        i32 = T.i32
++        pid = fx.block_idx.x
++        lane = fx.thread_idx.x
++        c_gqa = arith.constant(GQA, type=i32)
++        c_d = arith.constant(HEAD_DIM, type=i32)
++        c_splits = arith.constant(num_splits, type=i32)
++        c_zero = arith.constant(0.0, type=f32)
++        c_neg_inf = arith.constant(float("-inf"), type=f32)
++
++        q_head = arith.remui(_to_raw(pid), ArithValue(num_kv_heads) * c_gqa)
++        batch = arith.divui(_to_raw(pid), ArithValue(num_kv_heads) * c_gqa)
++        kv_head = arith.divui(q_head, c_gqa)
++        q_group = arith.remui(q_head, c_gqa)
++
++        po_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(partial_out, max_size=True)
++        pm_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(partial_max, max_size=True)
++        ps_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(partial_sum, max_size=True)
++        out_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource(output, max_size=True)
++
++        init = (c_neg_inf, c_zero, c_zero)
++        for split_i, state in range(0, num_splits, 1, init=init):
++            split = arith.index_cast(i32, _to_raw(split_i))
++            row = (
++                (
++                    (
++                        ArithValue(batch) * ArithValue(num_kv_heads) + kv_head
++                    )
++                    * c_splits
++                    + split
++                )
++                * c_gqa
++                + q_group
++            )
++            part_max = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                pm_rsrc, row, vec_width=1, dtype=f32
++            )
++            part_sum = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                ps_rsrc, row, vec_width=1, dtype=f32
++            )
++            part_out = buffer_ops.buffer_load(
++                po_rsrc, ArithValue(row) * c_d + lane, vec_width=1, dtype=f32
++            )
++
++            old_max, old_sum, old_out = state
++            valid = arith.cmpf(CmpFPredicate.OGT, part_sum, c_zero)
++            new_max = arith.maximumf(old_max, part_max)
++            first = arith.cmpf(CmpFPredicate.OEQ, old_max, c_neg_inf)
++            old_scale = arith.select(

++                arith.MulFOp(old_sum, old_scale, fastmath=fm_fast).result,

++                fastmath=fm_fast,

++            block_table_stride,

++                fx.Int64(batch_size)
++                * fx.Int64(num_kv_heads)
++                * num_splits,
++                1,
++                1,
++            ),
++            block=(BLOCK_THREADS, 1, 1),
++            stream=stream,
++        )
++        stage2(
++            partial_out,
++            partial_max,
++            partial_sum,
++            output,
++            batch_size,
++            num_kv_heads,

++            grid=(
++                fx.Int64(batch_size)
++                * fx.Int64(num_kv_heads)
++                * GQA,
++                1,
++                1,
++            ),
++            block=(BLOCK_THREADS, 1, 1),
++            stream=stream,
++        )
++

++
++@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
++def _launcher(num_splits: int, segment_size: int):
++    return _build_launcher(num_splits, segment_size)
++
++
++_SCRATCH_CACHE = {}
++
++
++def prepare_muse_paged_gqa_decode_scratch(
++    device: torch.device | str,
++    batches=range(1, 9),
++    num_kv_heads: int = 2,
++    num_splits: int = 128,
++):
++    """Preallocate graph-stable scratch for small Muse decode batches."""
++    device = torch.device(device)
++    for batch in batches:
++        key = (device, int(batch), num_kv_heads, num_splits)
++        if key in _SCRATCH_CACHE:
++            continue
++        rows = int(batch) * num_kv_heads * num_splits * GQA
++        partial_out = torch.empty(
++            rows, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
++        )
++        partial_max = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
++        partial_sum = torch.empty_like(partial_max)
++        _SCRATCH_CACHE[key] = (partial_out, partial_max, partial_sum)
++
++
++def muse_paged_gqa_decode_flydsl(
++    q: torch.Tensor,
++    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
++    v_cache: torch.Tensor,
++    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
++    block_table: torch.Tensor,
++    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
++    softmax_scale: float | None = None,
++    window_size: int = 2048,
++    num_splits: int = DEFAULT_NUM_SPLITS,
++    segment_size: int = DEFAULT_SEGMENT_SIZE,
++    scratch: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
++):
++    """Run the Muse-specialized FlyDSL split-K decode kernel.
++
++    Expected layouts:
++      q         [B, Hq, 64]
++      k/v cache [num_pages, 16, Hkv, 64]
++      table     [B, max_pages], int32
++    """
++    batch, num_q_heads, head_dim = q.shape
++    num_kv_heads = k_cache.shape[2]
++    if (
++        q.dtype != torch.bfloat16
++        or k_cache.dtype != torch.bfloat16
++        or v_cache.dtype != torch.bfloat16
++        or head_dim != HEAD_DIM
++        or k_cache.shape[1] != PAGE_SIZE
++        or num_q_heads != num_kv_heads * GQA
++        or seq_lens.dtype != torch.int64
++        or block_table.dtype != torch.int32
++    ):
++        raise ValueError(
++            "FlyDSL Muse decode requires BF16, d64, page16, GQA8 and int32 "
++            f"metadata; got q={q.dtype}/{tuple(q.shape)}, "
++            f"k={k_cache.dtype}/{tuple(k_cache.shape)}, "
++            f"v={v_cache.dtype}/{tuple(v_cache.shape)}, "
++            f"seq={seq_lens.dtype}/{tuple(seq_lens.shape)}, "
++            f"table={block_table.dtype}/{tuple(block_table.shape)}"
++        )
++    if out is None:
++        out = torch.empty_like(q)
++    if num_splits * segment_size < window_size:
++        raise ValueError("split coverage must be at least window_size")
++    rows = batch * num_kv_heads * num_splits * GQA
++    if scratch is None:
++        prepare_muse_paged_gqa_decode_scratch(
++            q.device,
++            batches=(batch,),
++            num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
++            num_splits=num_splits,
++        )
++        partial_out, partial_max, partial_sum = _SCRATCH_CACHE[
++            (q.device, batch, num_kv_heads, num_splits)
++        ]
++    else:
++        partial_out, partial_max, partial_sum = scratch
++    if softmax_scale is None:
++        softmax_scale = HEAD_DIM**-0.5
++    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(q.device).cuda_stream
++    _run_compiled(
++        _launcher(num_splits, segment_size),
++        q,
++        k_cache,
++        v_cache,
++        seq_lens,
++        block_table,
++        partial_out,
++        partial_max,
++        partial_sum,
++        out,
++        batch,
++        num_kv_heads,
++        block_table.stride(0),
++        window_size,
++        float(softmax_scale),
++        fx.Stream(stream),
++    )
++    return out, (partial_out, partial_max, partial_sum)
++

+# Muse Spark on MI355X: decode fusion passes (2026-09-07)
+
+Stack: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260905`, sglang dc28438 (+ patches/03 Plan B), aiter c16d44b9
+(+ patches/01), overlay = this repo (branch `rocm/decode-fusion`), TP8/EP8, `ATTN=aiter PAGE_SIZE=16`.
+Regression gate: gsm8k 1319q 5-shot (Accuracy 0.955-0.958 / Invalid 0 / 0 GPU faults on every run).
+Perf gate: fixed-length bench (`bench_e2e.py`, 256 tokens, ignore_eos) and per-bs `gen throughput` in the
+server log. gsm8k wall time is dominated by the longest greedy generations and is NOT a perf metric.
+
+## Why: decode was kernel-count bound
+Eager trace (BF16, conc 1): ~2,630 kernels per decode step (46.7/layer, ~8 us each); hipgraph replay wall
+(24.2 ms) ~= eager GPU busy (21 ms), i.e. the step is the sum of thousands of tiny kernels.
+Hot spots: RMSNorm decomposed into pow/mean/rsqrt/mul on the fp32 stream + `weight+gain` add per call,
+gated residual in eager, hipBLASLt skinny GEMMs with split-K reduce kernels, MoE glue, qk-norm + casts.
+
+## Passes (MXFP4 numbers, aiter prefill / Triton or 3D decode)
+| pass | change | conc1 step | fixed-256 bench conc 1/8/32/64/128 (tok/s) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| baseline | aligned stack, unfused | 20.9 ms | - (gsm8k 1280 tok/s) |
+| 1 | cached effective norm weights; cross-layer fused FFN boundary (`FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm` with next layer's pre_attn_norm / final norm) | 14.5 | - |
+| 2 | fused q/k RMSNorm(+scale) kernel; MXFP4 mid/large MoE tiles (16/64/256 G4, 64/64/128 G8 w4) | 14.0 | - |
+| 3 | MoE split-K=4 (<=32 slots) + one-program alignment (<=64 slots) + grid bound; BF16 small tile K128; mid/large crossover rows<=6144 (MXFP4) / 2048 (BF16) | 13.3 | 83/523/1654/2776/4045 |
+| 4a | fp32 router as split-K Triton GEMV (M<=64) | 12.85 | 86/539/1704/2820/4035 |
+| 4b | pooler/unpooler via aiter `tgemm.mm` at decode-sized M | 12.2 | 90/559/1750/2939/4043 |
+| +Plan B | decode on aiter unified-attention 3D (patches/03) instead of Triton decode | 11.8 | 92/566/1782/2993/4123 |
+BF16 pass 3: conc1 24.2 -> 14.6 ms, bench 75/378/1017/1659/2529 (weight-bandwidth bound at high conc).
+IL8192/OL128 conc4 (MXFP4, fused): Plan A TTFT 421 ms / TPOT 22.8 ms / 148.6 tok/s; Plan B 403 / 22.3 / 154.2.
+Kernels per layer: 46.7 -> ~24.
+
+## Switches (ROCm only; default on unless noted)
+`MUSE_FUSE_FFN_BOUNDARY`, `MUSE_FUSE_QK_NORM`, `MUSE_ROUTER_GEMV`, `MUSE_AITER_DENSE` (default off: slower than
+hipBLASLt on the pinned aiter), `MUSE_MOE_SPLITK` (4),
+`MUSE_MOE_ALIGN` (sgl|torch), `MUSE_MOE_FP4_MODE` (dot_scaled|manual), `MUSE_MOE_BACKEND` (triton|native|flydsl).
+`flydsl` needs `patches/04-aiter-muse-moe-flydsl.patch` on aiter `c16d44b9`.
+
+## Caveats
+- Norm effective weights and fused-op weight caches are computed in `post_load_weights`; a later weight
+  reload must call it again.
+- Eager micro-benchmarks of small kernels are CPU-launch bound on ROCm (~15 us/launch): time with CUDA-graph
+  replay. torch profiler cannot see hipgraph kernels; rocprofv3 wrapping the server aborts the HSA queue.
+- Standalone hipBLASLt shows algo-selection pathologies (e.g. 557 us at M=32) not seen inside the server.
+
+## Remaining per-layer budget at bs1 (~190 us): dense GEMMs ~65, MoE ~42, all-reduce ~30, attention ~20,
+router ~12, norms/glue ~20. Next: aiter tuner entries for qkv/pooler/unpooler shapes (asm), aiter MoE stage2
+without top-k combine (needs aiter change), Plan C FlyDSL SWA decode, all-reduce+norm fusion.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""CPU-only structural checks for the Muse MoE FlyDSL performance plan."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SOURCE = Path("sglang_meta_common/sglang_meta_common/ops/muse_moe_flydsl.py")
+SELECTOR_NAMES = {
+    "_SMALL_M",
+    "_MID_M",
+    "_LARGE_M",
+    "_SMALL_M_FP4",
+    "_MID_M_FP4",
+    "_LARGE_M_FP4",
+    "_pick_flydsl_config",
+}
+
+
+def selector_from_text(text: str):
+    tree = ast.parse(text)
+    selected = []
+    for node in tree.body:
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)):
+            targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else [node.target]
+            if any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id in SELECTOR_NAMES for t in targets):
+                selected.append(node)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in SELECTOR_NAMES:
+            selected.append(node)
+    module = ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=selected, type_ignores=[]))
+    namespace: dict[str, object] = {}
+    exec(compile(module, str(SOURCE), "exec"), namespace)
+    return namespace["_pick_flydsl_config"]
+
+
+def git_text(revision: str) -> str:
+    return subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "show", f"{revision}:{SOURCE.as_posix()}"],
+        check=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    ).stdout
+
+
+def lds_bytes(
+    dtype: str, block_m: int, block_n: int, block_k: int, halves: int, stages: int
+) -> dict[str, int]:
+    activation = stages * block_m * block_k * 2
+    if dtype == "mxfp4":
+        weight = stages * halves * block_n * block_k // 2
+        scales = stages * halves * block_n * block_k // 32
+    else:
+        weight = stages * halves * block_n * block_k * 2
+        scales = 0
+    return {
+        "activation": activation,
+        "weight": weight,
+        "scales": scales,
+        "total": activation + weight + scales,
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--baseline", default="a29522f")
+    parser.add_argument("--pre-change", default="a29522f^")
+    parser.add_argument("--emit-manifest", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    current_text = SOURCE.read_text()
+    compile(current_text, str(SOURCE), "exec")
+    current, baseline = (
+        selector_from_text(current_text),
+        selector_from_text(git_text(args.baseline)),
+    )
+    pre_change = selector_from_text(git_text(args.pre_change))
+
+    for m in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128):
+        for mxfp4 in (False, True):
+            for topk, experts in ((2, 8), (8, 32)):
+                actual = current(m, topk, experts, mxfp4)
+                expected = baseline(m, topk, experts, mxfp4)
+                if mxfp4 or m > 16:
+                    assert actual == expected, (m, mxfp4, expected, actual)
+                    assert actual == pre_change(m, topk, experts, mxfp4), (
+                        m,
+                        mxfp4,
+                        actual,
+                    )
+                elif m <= 4:
+                    assert actual["BLOCK_N"] == 16
+                    assert actual["FLYDSL_K_UNROLL"] == 4
+                    assert actual["FLYDSL_SPLIT_K"] == 4
+                else:
+                    assert actual["BLOCK_N"] == 64 and actual["num_warps"] == 4
+                    assert actual["GEMM1_FLYDSL_K_UNROLL"] == 2
+                    assert actual["GEMM2_FLYDSL_K_UNROLL"] == 4
+                assert "GEMM2_BLOCK_N" not in actual, (m, actual)
+    for m in (256, 512, 1024):
+        cfg = current(m, 2, 8, True)
+        assert cfg["GEMM2_BLOCK_N"] == 256, (m, cfg)
+        assert cfg["FLYDSL_K_UNROLL"] == 16 and cfg["num_warps"] == 2, (m, cfg)
+    for m in (129, 1024):
+        assert current(m, 8, 32, True).get("GEMM2_BLOCK_N") == 256
+        assert "GEMM2_BLOCK_N" not in current(m, 8, 32, False)
+    assert "GEMM2_BLOCK_N" not in current(1025, 8, 32, True)
+
+    status_stream = sys.stderr if args.emit_manifest else sys.stdout
+    print(
+        f"selector: MXFP4 boundaries match {args.baseline} and {args.pre_change}; BF16 M=4 split-K and M=8/16 candidates checked",
+        file=status_stream,
+    )
+    print(
+        "selector: MXFP4 M=256/512/1024 uses GEMM2 BN256, unroll16, warps2",
+        file=status_stream,
+    )
+    for dtype in ("bf16", "mxfp4"):
+        for stage, bn, halves in (("gemm1", 128, 2), ("gemm2", 256, 1)):
+            sizes = [
+                lds_bytes(dtype, 16, bn, bk, halves, 2)["total"] // 1024
+                for bk in (64, 128, 512)
+            ]
+            print(
+                f"{dtype} {stage} BN={bn}: BK64/128/512 = {sizes} KiB",
+                file=status_stream,
+            )
+    if args.emit_manifest:
+        base = [
+            "python",
+            "/home/yichiche/flydsl-work/bench_muse_moe_flydsl.py",
+            "--rows",
+            "4",
+            "8",
+            "16",
+            "32",
+            "64",
+            "128",
+            "256",
+            "--experts",
+            "32",
+        ]
+        manifest = []
+        for dtype in ("bf16", "mxfp4"):
+            for local_slots in (1, 2, 4, 8):
+                common = base + ["--dtype", dtype, "--local-slots", str(local_slots)]
+                if dtype == "mxfp4":
+                    common += ["--random-scales"]
+                manifest.append(
+                    {
+                        "format": dtype,
+                        "stage": "control",
+                        "local_slots": local_slots,
+                        "argv": common,
+                    }
+                )
+                if dtype == "bf16":
+                    for stage in ("gemm1", "gemm2"):
+                        for bn in (32, 64, 128):
+                            argv = common + [
+                                f"--{stage}-block-n",
+                                str(bn),
+                                f"--{stage}-num-warps",
+                                "4",
+                            ]
+                            manifest.append(
+                                {
+                                    "format": dtype,
+                                    "stage": stage,
+                                    "local_slots": local_slots,
+                                    "candidate": {"block_n": bn, "warps": 4},
+                                    "argv": argv,
+                                }
+                            )
+        print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
